Sanjay: ran the nomad multi-region sweep for mosaic-7b across A100/H100, int8/int4, and we have a few surprising bits. posting raw numbers and quick takeaways. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maria: awesome, drop the table pls — will use for capacity planning.
Sanjay: here's the condensed CSV from the runs (seq=1024, batch=4, workload=chat-like prefill+decode mix):
```
region,gpu,quant,prefill_p50_ms,decode_ms_per_token,tokens_per_sec,$_per_1M_tokens,kernel
us-west-2,H100,int8,410,0.00105,950,6.8,flash-attn-v2
us-west-2,A100,int8,480,0.00143,700,9.5,ref-cuda
eu-west-1,H100,int8,430,0.00112,880,7.2,flash-attn-v2
eu-west-1,A100,int8,510,0.00150,640,10.4,ref-cuda
ap-northeast-1,H100,int8,460,0.00120,820,7.9,flash-attn-v2
ap-northeast-1,A100,int8,530,0.00155,610,11.0,ref-cuda
us-west-2,H100,int4,420,0.00090,1120,5.8,flash-attn-v2
us-west-2,A100,int4,495,0.00120,830,8.1,ref-cuda
```
Sanjay: TL;DR: H100 gives ~30-60% higher tokens/sec vs A100 for these configs, and tails are tighter. int4 is faster but we saw quality drift on long-context tests.
Kevin: concrete numbers for $/1M tokens look great on H100 — did you include amortized infra (eg slab pricing) or pure cloud spot on-demand?
Sanjay: these are modeled on our Dedicated pricing (amortized monthly GPU cost + network egress + perf overheads). Not spot. I also computed a conservative hosted estimate (+20%).
Maria: on the kernels — looks like H100 is hitting flash-attn-v2 consistently, while A100 fell back to ref-cuda for some sequence-lengths. that's probably the big perf delta right?
Sanjay: yep. observed fallback on A100 when seq>=1024 and batch>=4 for a couple operator patterns. that drives the prefill p50 up and decode per-token ms up too.
Jen: quality: what's the eval delta between fp16/int8/int4? any regressions above our threshold?
Sanjay: ran eval-suite v3 (synthetic Qs + real user prompt set). int8: mean ROUGE/ExactMatch drop ~0.6% vs fp16 — within threshold. int4: drop ~3.8% overall and notable failures on long-code-completion prompts (context > 2k).
Maria: so int8 is a keeper for Mosaic-7b on these workloads, int4 is still risky for prod.
Kevin: p95/p99 tails? we care about spikes for latency SLOs.
Sanjay: p95 for H100 decode was ~42 ms total (including transfer), p99 ~85 ms. A100 p95 ~73 ms, p99 ~160 ms. tails double when kernel fallback happens.
bench-bot: run complete: job_id=nomad-sweep-1755, artifacts -> s3://redwood-bench/nomad/1755554321/
ops-bot: noticed increased cpu on host side when using int4 on A100 due to emulation path (tracked in infra ticket INF-3342).
Jen: can we summarize actionable changes?
Maria: my notes —
- Default production SKU for mosaic-7b: H100 int8 where available (region aware routing).
- Fallback policy: if H100 unavailable, route to A100 int8 with reduced batch size to avoid kernel fallback.
- Disable int4 for user-facing default until long-context evals pass (flagged).
- Update model catalog pricing and perf numbers (include $/1M tokens per region).
Kevin: add autoscaler tweak: lower max-batch to 2 for A100 fallbacks to keep decode latency under SLO.
Sanjay: I'll open two PRs: one to the routing policy (add region-pref H100-int8) and one to the perf docs.
Jen: please also add an eval alert: when int8 quality drops >1% on the longtail prompt set, notify eng-ml.
Sanjay: filing tickets: RT-1127 (routing + pricing), RT-1128 (eval alert), INF-3342 (cpu emulation), DOCS-749 (perf doc update).
Maria: quick sanity check — are these numbers stable across runs? variance?
Sanjay: ran 5 repeats over 24h window. stdev tokens/sec H100 ~4.2%, A100 ~6.8% (higher because of fallbacks). no huge outliers except one thermal throttle on a rack in ap-northeast-1 (we excluded that run).
Kevin: do we want to pre-warm KV caches in EU for lower prefill p50?
Jen: yes for critical customers — add warmup policy per model in Redwood Console.
Maria: I'll draft the console change. tagging @Kevin for autoscale tweak, @Sanjay for PRs.
Kevin: +1. thanks for the sweep, Sanjay. this is exactly the data we needed for next week's capacity sync. :rocket:
Jen: can someone add a short note in the release channel once DOCS-749 merges? I'll coordinate comms to customers.
Sanjay: will do. thanks all.
